meta.title: Operation of Bacterial Incubator in Microbiology Laboratory

sections.purpose: To maintain controlled temperature conditions (35–37°C for bacterial cultures; 25–28°C for fungal cultures) for optimal growth of microorganisms in pharmaceutical microbiology experiments.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Microbiology laboratory for incubation of bacterial and fungal cultures, sterility testing incubation, antimicrobial susceptibility testing plates, and microbial limit testing samples.
procedure: Switch on the bacterial incubator and set the thermostat to the required temperature: 35–37°C for pathogenic and pharmaceutical bacteria; 30–32°C for environmental bacteria; 25–28°C for fungi and yeasts.
Allow the incubator to equilibrate at the set temperature for a minimum of 30 minutes before loading cultures.
Verify the internal temperature with a calibrated thermometer placed at mid-shelf level — do not rely solely on the thermostat dial.
Before loading, ensure all culture vessels are labelled: organism name/code, culture medium, date of inoculation, expected incubation period, and operator.
Place inoculated Petri dishes inverted (agar side up) to prevent condensation from dropping onto colonies.
Space plates and tubes with adequate clearance to allow air circulation — do not overcrowd.
Do not mix different organism categories in the same incubator during critical experiments (e.g., sterility testing cultures should be isolated).
Record loading time, organisms, and incubation parameters in the incubator log.
Record temperature twice daily (morning and afternoon) in the temperature monitoring log.
After the incubation period, remove cultures and proceed to examination without delay.
Log the removal time and observations (confluent growth, colony count, colour, morphology).
After use, wipe the interior of the incubator with a 70% ethanol-dampened cloth; allow to dry before the next use.
Perform deep cleaning with an appropriate disinfectant monthly.
precautions: Never place open or unsealed culture containers in the incubator — aerosol generation causes cross-contamination.
All incubation of potential pathogens must be in sealed containers.
Do not open the incubator door frequently — each opening causes temperature fluctuation and extends equilibration time.
Install a temperature alarm (min/max thermometer with alarm) to alert if temperature deviates outside the set range.
Calibrate the incubator thermostat against a reference thermometer every 6 months.
Maintain the incubator humidity by placing a tray of water inside if drying of agar plates is a concern.
Restrict access to authorized personnel — keep incubator door locked when not in supervised use.
